transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You favor one side when you stand, boy. The stone noticed before I did; it always does. Tell me what you are hiding, or keep hiding it and say why you came this far anyway.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It is... nothing, I just need my brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Nothing makes the body lie like that. Your weight drags to the left, and your breath breaks before it should. Say more about your brother, then, since you will not say more about yourself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I dared him... and the hand took him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Yes. I know whose hand that was, and what it answers to. Continue. What did your daring taste like in your mouth when you spoke it, and what did you do after the well answered you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It was just... a joke... then I jumped.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A joke does not bend a leg like that when it lands. You jumped after him, and the ground argued with you; I can hear it in your pauses. Say it properly—what did you feel when you hit, and why did you keep moving after?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I heard... a crack, but I can't stop.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A crack is not nothing, and it is not quiet. Bone remembers being broken even when the mouth refuses. You say you cannot stop—tell me what you think will happen if you do.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: If I stop... I lose him forever.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Forever is a heavy word to limp on. Your body is already paying it, step by step, and still you lean forward. Tell me exactly where you think he is now, if stopping makes him vanish.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He is... somewhere behind your golden gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Behind it, yes—but not erased by your pause, nor rescued by your bleeding haste. You believe motion itself keeps him alive; that is what I hear. Say more, boy—why does standing still feel like betrayal to you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Because... I am the reason... he was taken.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Reason is a sharp thing to kneel on, and you are pressing your weight into it as hard as that injured side will allow. Guilt makes people move when wisdom would make them listen. Tell me why punishment through pain feels fair to you, and why saving him must look like this.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... deserve to feel what he feels.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No. You are guessing at his pain and choosing a shape for it that fits your guilt. That is colder than mercy, and lazier than love. What do you think he feels right now—say it exactly, not what you think you deserve.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He feels... terrified... and thinks... I abandoned him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You imagine his fear wearing your face, accusing you with every breath. Yet you are here, cracked and upright, arguing with a gate instead of turning back. Why does it matter so much to you that he believes you came, even if it costs you the use of that leg?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He has to know... I didn't leave him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You keep saying *has to*, as if the stone itself commanded you. That leg shakes when you speak like that; even your breath leans around it. Tell me—when did you decide that proving this mattered more than what it would cost you?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: The second... I heard him scream.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That scream still rings inside the break; I can hear how you set your weight around it. You decided instantly, without bargaining, without checking what would tear. Say more—what did your body do in that second before your mind followed?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... just threw myself... in.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: So the well did not take you cleanly—you met it halfway. Stone, or the fall itself, chose a place to mark you. Tell me how it happened, plainly, and where it hurts when you pretend it does not.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I hit... the wall... my ribs... burn with every breath.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Ribs then. That is why your words arrive in pieces, why you bargain with air before each one. Did you keep going immediately after, or did you wait there pressed to stone deciding whether pain was permission to stop?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I didn't wait... I just... kept climbing.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Of course you did. Even broken breath was not enough to slow you. What did you use to climb with ribs screaming like that—hands, feet, blood, or memory?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My fingers... just dug in... until they bled.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You chose grip over breath, and let the rock drink first. Blood is honest that way. When your fingers split and slid, whose name did you think, or did you climb without words at all?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just... his name... over and over.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: That is a narrow prayer, repeated until it cuts. You did not ask for strength, only kept his name between you and the dark. When the pain sharpened and the rock answered with more of itself, did you ever think of turning back—or did the thought never form?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I couldn't... go back... without him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then the choice was finished before it began. Not bravery—closure. Tell me this last thing about it: when your ribs burned and your fingers opened, did you know you might not reach him, or did that knowledge arrive only after you were already climbing?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... didn't let myself... think it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No. You sealed the thought away and climbed on what was left of you. That is not hope; it is refusal, and it irritates me more than fear ever has. The gold is quiet today, the gate forgets to be closed, and I find I have nothing else to ask you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... have to... go in.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You were already inside the moment you jumped, boy. Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My leg... is fine... I'm going.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then stand as long as you can, and longer than that. The way opens because you would have walked it even if I had stayed silent.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just... one step... then another.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Yes. One step that does not ask permission, then the next that forgets to be afraid. The gold parts for you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... just... need to see him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then see him. The gate no longer remembers being shut.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... won't... leave him here.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You never were.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm... coming... for... you... Omar.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... won't... stop... walking.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just... a... few... more... steps.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then take them. The path does not test you anymore, and neither do I.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: My... leg... burns... but... I... walk.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
Yes. You would have burned down to bone and still leaned forward.  
That is enough.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... won't... fall... until... I... hold... him.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Then do not fall. The gold is already wide, and it does not wait for you to thank it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... didn't... come... for... the... gold.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text:
I know. That is why it moved.  
Go.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I... won't... leave... him... here.
